actions.name: Create a modular account with OwnableValidator
actions.summary: The room agrees owners and a threshold; a factory deploys an ERC-7579 account with OwnableValidator installed, through the first UserOperation's initCode. The account implementation (Safe7579, Nexus, Kernel …) is the member's choice.

fields.name: factory
fields.means: the account factory named in initCode

fields.name: factoryData
fields.means: the factory call, including the account implementation and its modules

fields.name: owners
fields.means: the owner addresses, sorted ascending and unique, at most 32

fields.name: threshold
fields.means: k, between 1 and the owner count

fields.name: initData
fields.means: abi.encode(threshold, owners), passed to OwnableValidator.onInstall

fields.name: nonce
fields.means: the EntryPoint nonce: a 192-bit key and a 64-bit sequence; many accounts put the validator's address in the key (Safe7579: the top 20 bytes)

fields.name: callGasLimit
fields.means: gas for the execution call

fields.name: verificationGasLimit
fields.means: gas for validation

fields.name: preVerificationGas
fields.means: gas the bundler charges for calldata and overhead

fields.name: maxFeePerGas
fields.means: EIP-1559 fee cap per gas

fields.name: maxPriorityFeePerGas
fields.means: EIP-1559 tip per gas

fields.name: paymasterAndData
fields.means: empty unless a paymaster pays; hashed into userOpHash either way

fields.name: entryPoint
fields.means: the EntryPoint the account accepts; hashed into userOpHash

agreement.threshold: k of n of the new owners sign the first UserOp
agreement.domain: EIP-191 personal_sign of the first UserOp's userOpHash (commits to keccak256(initCode))

requirements.name: bundler
requirements.target: an ERC-7769 bundler endpoint for the account's EntryPoint

requirements.name: gas-prefund
requirements.target: the counterfactual account address, or a paymaster

disclosure.field: owner addresses shared by each member
unsigned first UserOp with initCode: owners, threshold (bundler, gas estimation)
owner signatures in the handleOps calldata (who signed)

steps.does: each future owner shares a signing address; the proposer composes owners (sorted, unique), threshold and the factory call; the room computes the counterfactual address and discloses the account (S1) as pending
k of the new owners re-derive the first UserOp's userOpHash, which commits to keccak256(initCode), and sign
steps.signs: EIP-191 personal_sign of the 32-byte userOpHash: ECDSA(secp256k1) over keccak256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n32" || userOpHash). On EntryPoint v0.7, userOpHash = keccak256(abi.encode(keccak256(abi.encode(sender, nonce, keccak256(initCode), keccak256(callData), accountGasLimits, preVerificationGas, gasFees, keccak256(paymasterAndData))), entryPoint, chainId)); on v0.8+ it is the EIP-712 hash with domain {name "ERC4337", version "1", chainId, verifyingContract = entryPoint}. One 65-byte r || s || v (v = 27/28) per owner

steps.does: a member sends the first UserOp; the EntryPoint runs initCode through the factory, the account installs OwnableValidator (onInstall stores owners and threshold keyed by the account), then validates the owner signatures
steps.signs: nothing new; the member concatenates at least threshold owner signatures into userOp.signature (order does not matter: the validator sorts and de-duplicates signers) and sends the UserOp with eth_sendUserOperation

steps.does: reads getOwners, threshold and the installed modules back from the chain and marks the disclosure verified

refusals.what: an initCode the room did not derive from the agreed owners, threshold and factory call
refusals.why: invariant 1: userOpHash commits to keccak256(initCode); another initCode deploys another account

refusals.what: owners not sorted and unique, a threshold of 0 or above the owner count, or more than 32 owners
refusals.why: OwnableValidator.onInstall reverts NotSortedAndUnique / ThresholdNotSet / InvalidThreshold / MaxOwnersReached; muster refuses at propose

refusals.what: a factory that installs other validators or executors the card does not show
refusals.why: they are ways around the owners' threshold; an unread module list is an unaccounted input (invariant 10)

claims.claim: The address is fixed by the factory call before anything is on chain.
The owners and threshold are public on chain from deployment (OwnerAdded, ModuleInitialized events).
The bundler sees the future account's owners when it estimates the first UserOp.

evidence.what: OwnableValidator.onInstall: abi.decode(data, (uint256 threshold, address[] owners)); sorted and unique; at most 32; threshold ≤ owners
ERC-7579: installModule MUST call onInstall with initData and emit ModuleInstalled
ERC-4337: first-time account creation through initCode (factory || factoryData)
EntryPoint v0.7.0 UserOperationLib.encode hashes keccak256(initCode) into userOp.hash()

unverified: Which EntryPoint version (v0.7 or v0.8+) a given ERC-7579 account implementation targets; the signed hash differs between them.
Validator selection is account-specific (ERC-7579 does not dictate it); only Safe7579's nonce-key encoding was checked here, not Nexus or Kernel.
Production maturity and audit scope of OwnableValidator (carried from the registry).

actions.name: Send ETH from a modular account
actions.summary: k of n OwnableValidator owners approve a UserOperation whose callData is execute(single call, to, value); one member hands it to a bundler.

fields.name: account
fields.means: the ERC-7579 account that acts (the UserOp sender)

fields.name: to
fields.means: the payee's address

fields.name: value
fields.means: the amount of ETH, in wei

fields.name: mode
fields.means: ERC-7579 execution mode: callType 0x00 (single call), execType 0x00 (revert on failure)

fields.name: nonce
fields.means: the EntryPoint nonce: a 192-bit key and a 64-bit sequence; many accounts put the validator's address in the key (Safe7579: the top 20 bytes)

fields.name: callGasLimit
fields.means: gas for the execution call

fields.name: verificationGasLimit
fields.means: gas for validation

fields.name: preVerificationGas
fields.means: gas the bundler charges for calldata and overhead

fields.name: maxFeePerGas
fields.means: EIP-1559 fee cap per gas

fields.name: maxPriorityFeePerGas
fields.means: EIP-1559 tip per gas

fields.name: paymasterAndData
fields.means: empty unless a paymaster pays; hashed into userOpHash either way

fields.name: entryPoint
fields.means: the EntryPoint the account accepts; hashed into userOpHash

agreement.threshold: k of n owners (the validator's threshold, read from the chain)
agreement.domain: EIP-191 personal_sign of the ERC-4337 userOpHash (commits to entryPoint and chainId)

requirements.name: bundler
requirements.target: an ERC-7769 bundler endpoint for the account's EntryPoint

disclosure.field: account address, nonce key and balance reads
unsigned UserOp: sender, nonce, callData, gas fields (bundler, eth_estimateUserOperationGas)
signed UserOp with owner signatures (bundler, eth_sendUserOperation)
owner signatures in the handleOps calldata (who signed)
the bundler's address and beneficiary; gas paid

steps.does: composes the effect; callData = execute(mode, abi.encodePacked(to, value, "")); reads the nonce for the validator's key and fees through the RPC; the bundler estimates gas; the room re-derives userOpHash
each owner re-derives userOpHash from the effect and signs it; a hardware wallet shows only the 32-byte hash, so the room's re-derived view is the only readable one
steps.signs: EIP-191 personal_sign of the 32-byte userOpHash: ECDSA(secp256k1) over keccak256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n32" || userOpHash). On EntryPoint v0.7, userOpHash = keccak256(abi.encode(keccak256(abi.encode(sender, nonce, keccak256(initCode), keccak256(callData), accountGasLimits, preVerificationGas, gasFees, keccak256(paymasterAndData))), entryPoint, chainId)); on v0.8+ it is the EIP-712 hash with domain {name "ERC4337", version "1", chainId, verifyingContract = entryPoint}. One 65-byte r || s || v (v = 27/28) per owner

steps.does: one member sends the UserOp to the bundler; the bundler simulates it (ERC-7562) and calls EntryPoint.handleOps; the account selects the validator (account-specific; Safe7579 reads it from the nonce key) and calls OwnableValidator.validateUserOp, which recovers threshold signers over toEthSignedMessageHash(userOpHash), counts distinct owners, and returns success or failure; the account then runs the callData
steps.signs: nothing new; the member concatenates at least threshold owner signatures into userOp.signature (order does not matter: the validator sorts and de-duplicates signers) and sends the UserOp with eth_sendUserOperation

steps.does: reads eth_getUserOperationReceipt from the bundler, or the UserOperationEvent through the RPC; final when the chain is

refusals.what: an owner signature over a userOpHash that is not the one the room re-derives from the effect
refusals.why: invariant 1 (F-4): refuse on mismatch; the owner's device shows only the hash, so this check is the review

refusals.what: a userOpHash computed for a different chainId or EntryPoint than the disclosed account's
refusals.why: invariant 2 (F-5): userOpHash commits to entryPoint and chainId; a mismatch binds the signature elsewhere

refusals.what: a nonce whose key names a validator other than the OwnableValidator the account disclosed, on accounts that select the validator from the nonce
refusals.why: invariant 2: the nonce key is the slot; on Safe7579 a key naming no installed validator falls back to the Safe's own owners

refusals.what: a stale nonce: the (key, sequence) pair was consumed since the proposal, re-read at review and at settle
refusals.why: invariant 10: the nonce is an external read that reached the signed bytes

refusals.what: any gas, fee or paymaster input that reached the UserOp without a recorded read
refusals.why: invariant 10: nothing is signed whose inputs cannot be accounted for

refusals.what: counting two signatures from the same owner, or a signer the validator does not list
refusals.why: invariant 9 and the validator itself: signers are sorted, de-duplicated and checked against the owner list

claims.claim: Owners sign userOpHash, which covers every UserOp field except the signature, the EntryPoint and the chain id.
An owner signing on a hardware wallet sees only an opaque 32-byte hash; what they approve is what their muster client shows them.
Other installed validators and executors can act on the account without these owners' threshold.
claims.party: every other installed validator or executor module (on Safe7579, also the Safe's own owners)

claims.claim: The bundler can delay or refuse to include the UserOp.
The bundler sees the signed UserOp, including which owners signed, before the chain does.
OwnableValidator puts no validity window on owner signatures: collected signatures stay valid until the nonce is used.
claims.party: anyone holding the assembled UserOp (room members; the bundler once sent)

claims.claim: Approving costs owners nothing; the account prefunds gas to the EntryPoint.

actions.name: Install or uninstall a module on a modular account

fields.means: installModule | uninstallModule

fields.name: moduleTypeId
fields.means: 1 validator, 2 executor, 3 fallback handler, 4 hook

fields.name: module
fields.means: the module's address

fields.name: initData
fields.means: passed to onInstall / onUninstall; decoded on the card when the module is known

fields.name: nonce
fields.means: the EntryPoint nonce: a 192-bit key and a 64-bit sequence; many accounts put the validator's address in the key (Safe7579: the top 20 bytes)

fields.name: callGasLimit
fields.means: gas for the execution call

fields.name: verificationGasLimit
fields.means: gas for validation

fields.name: preVerificationGas
fields.means: gas the bundler charges for calldata and overhead

fields.name: maxFeePerGas
fields.means: EIP-1559 fee cap per gas

fields.name: maxPriorityFeePerGas
fields.means: EIP-1559 tip per gas

fields.name: paymasterAndData
fields.means: empty unless a paymaster pays; hashed into userOpHash either way

fields.name: entryPoint
fields.means: the EntryPoint the account accepts; hashed into userOpHash

agreement.threshold: k of n owners (the validator's threshold, read from the chain)
agreement.domain: EIP-191 personal_sign of the ERC-4337 userOpHash (commits to entryPoint and chainId)

requirements.name: bundler

steps.does: composes the change; callData = installModule(moduleTypeId, module, initData) or uninstallModule(...), which ERC-7579 requires the account to authorize (onlyEntryPointOrSelf); reads the module's code and isModuleType(moduleTypeId) through the RPC; the room re-derives userOpHash
each owner re-derives userOpHash from the effect and signs it; a hardware wallet shows only the 32-byte hash, so the room's re-derived view is the only readable one
steps.signs: EIP-191 personal_sign of the 32-byte userOpHash: ECDSA(secp256k1) over keccak256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n32" || userOpHash). On EntryPoint v0.7, userOpHash = keccak256(abi.encode(keccak256(abi.encode(sender, nonce, keccak256(initCode), keccak256(callData), accountGasLimits, preVerificationGas, gasFees, keccak256(paymasterAndData))), entryPoint, chainId)); on v0.8+ it is the EIP-712 hash with domain {name "ERC4337", version "1", chainId, verifyingContract = entryPoint}. One 65-byte r || s || v (v = 27/28) per owner

steps.does: one member sends the UserOp to the bundler; the bundler simulates it (ERC-7562) and calls EntryPoint.handleOps; the account selects the validator (account-specific; Safe7579 reads it from the nonce key) and calls OwnableValidator.validateUserOp, which recovers threshold signers over toEthSignedMessageHash(userOpHash), counts distinct owners, and returns success or failure; the account then runs the callData
steps.signs: nothing new; the member concatenates at least threshold owner signatures into userOp.signature (order does not matter: the validator sorts and de-duplicates signers) and sends the UserOp with eth_sendUserOperation

steps.does: reads eth_getUserOperationReceipt from the bundler, or the UserOperationEvent through the RPC; final when the chain is

refusals.what: an owner signature over a userOpHash that is not the one the room re-derives from the effect
refusals.why: invariant 1 (F-4): refuse on mismatch; the owner's device shows only the hash, so this check is the review

refusals.what: a userOpHash computed for a different chainId or EntryPoint than the disclosed account's
refusals.why: invariant 2 (F-5): userOpHash commits to entryPoint and chainId; a mismatch binds the signature elsewhere

refusals.what: a nonce whose key names a validator other than the OwnableValidator the account disclosed, on accounts that select the validator from the nonce
refusals.why: invariant 2: the nonce key is the slot; on Safe7579 a key naming no installed validator falls back to the Safe's own owners

refusals.what: a stale nonce: the (key, sequence) pair was consumed since the proposal, re-read at review and at settle
refusals.why: invariant 10: the nonce is an external read that reached the signed bytes

refusals.what: any gas, fee or paymaster input that reached the UserOp without a recorded read
refusals.why: invariant 10: nothing is signed whose inputs cannot be accounted for

refusals.what: counting two signatures from the same owner, or a signer the validator does not list
refusals.why: invariant 9 and the validator itself: signers are sorted, de-duplicated and checked against the owner list

refusals.what: a module whose isModuleType(moduleTypeId) is false, or whose code was not read
refusals.why: invariant 10: the meaning of the proposal depends on an external read; ERC-7579 requires accounts to keep module types apart

claims.claim: Owners sign userOpHash, which covers every UserOp field except the signature, the EntryPoint and the chain id.
An owner signing on a hardware wallet sees only an opaque 32-byte hash; what they approve is what their muster client shows them.
Other installed validators and executors can act on the account without these owners' threshold.
claims.party: every other installed validator or executor module (on Safe7579, also the Safe's own owners)

claims.claim: The bundler can delay or refuse to include the UserOp.
The bundler sees the signed UserOp, including which owners signed, before the chain does.
OwnableValidator puts no validity window on owner signatures: collected signatures stay valid until the nonce is used.
claims.party: anyone holding the assembled UserOp (room members; the bundler once sent)

claims.claim: Approving costs owners nothing; the account prefunds gas to the EntryPoint.
An installed executor can call executeFromExecutor and act without the owners' threshold.
An installed hook can revert every execution and lock the account.
Uninstalling OwnableValidator clears its owners and threshold for this account (onUninstall).

evidence.what: ERC-7579 (Draft): execute / installModule / uninstallModule, module types 1–4, execution mode encoding; validator selection left to the account
OwnableValidator: onInstall(abi.encode(threshold, owners)), MAX_OWNERS = 32, validateUserOp over ECDSA.toEthSignedMessageHash(userOpHash)
CheckNSignatures.recoverNSignatures: threshold 65-byte r||s||v signatures; v = 0 contract signature, v > 30 eth_sign
modulekit ERC7579ValidatorBase: VALIDATION_SUCCESS = 0, VALIDATION_FAILED = 1 (no validity window)
Safe7579 adapter: validator := shr(96, nonce); an uninstalled validator falls back to Safe.checkSignatures
ERC-4337: UserOperation, userOpHash commits to chainid and EntryPoint, the 2D nonce, bundlers
EntryPoint v0.7.0: getUserOpHash = keccak256(abi.encode(userOp.hash(), address(this), block.chainid))
EntryPoint v0.7.0 UserOperationLib.encode: the fields hashed into userOp.hash()
EntryPoint v0.8.0: userOpHash is EIP-712 with domain name "ERC4337", version "1"
ERC-7769: the bundler JSON-RPC API
EIP-191: signed data standard (personal_sign prefix)

unverified: Registry lists expiry as optional (ERC-4337 validationData can carry validUntil/validAfter), but OwnableValidator.validateUserOp returns VALIDATION_SUCCESS (0) or VALIDATION_FAILED (1) with no window; only a paymaster or a pre-validation hook could bound the owners' signatures.
Which EntryPoint version (v0.7 or v0.8+) a given ERC-7579 account implementation targets; the signed hash differs between them.
Validator selection is account-specific (ERC-7579 does not dictate it); only Safe7579's nonce-key encoding was checked here, not Nexus or Kernel.
Production maturity and audit scope of OwnableValidator (carried from the registry).
